doc.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020

title: Basie versus Buddy Rich at 21
summary: Asked a hypothetical, Bergeron says he would choose Basie, loves Sammy Nestico charts, and admits he was not ready then.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Speaking of a 30-year-old Wayne, I’m going to go back a little farther than that and create a fictional scenario. If you were 21 or 2, and you got a call to sub on lead trumpet with the Count Basie orchestra on a Sunday, and then you got, unbelievably, a second call to sub on lead trumpet on the Buddy Rich orchestra the next day, what would be the difference in those gigs as far as playing lead trumpet?

Well I would have picked Count Basie’s band and said no to Buddy first of all. Because it’s funny you should mention Count Basie because of any name band that I would have ever wanted to really play — I mean I would have liked to play with any of them. But to play with Count Basie, in that band, because that’s the music that moves my soul. You know I do a lot of other things to make a living but my wife will tell you when I’m playing, you know, a Billy Byers’ chart, or a Frank Foster chart, or a Sammy Nestico chart, I just go Pffw — here we go. This is my shit. You know? And I just can sink my teeth into it and they’re playable. They’re difficult but there’s no pyrotechnics involved it’s just all about feel and about where you put the time and going through high school my band director was all about Count Basie. So in the 70s, that’s when Sammy Nestico was writing a lot. He’d written a lot for the Count Basie band in the late 60s. So all those charts that came, “Basie Straight Ahead” and all those things that we know and love, I grew up and started playing, my first chart I ever played in junior high was a watered down version of “The Queen Bee.” The first big band chart I ever played. Sammy Nestico chart. So I’ve always just kind of loved that music and it’s embedded in me, and so that kind of music is what moves my soul. And I loved Buddy Rich too, and Buddy Rich had a swinging band. But there was something about that other thing. And to answer your question, at 21 I would have had to say no and I think I was even smart enough to realize I wasn’t ready musically.

I wasn’t ready, at 21 years old I wasn’t ready. I could have been if I would have paid more attention through high school. And it’s almost a problem that I had some natural ability because I let that carry me through as far as it could, and I wasn’t working on my craft, and I wasn’t practicing enough, and I wasn’t listening enough. I could do the things I had to do and I could play a Basie chart pretty good because I kind of knew it. But you know to really, I didn’t have the — at 21 I didn’t have the maturity of time or any of that I don’t think to have sat with that band and done the lead chair justice. And Buddy’s band would have probably just chewed me up and spit me out you know.
